svg.title: Motherbricks security trust boundaries and data classification
svg.desc: Motherbricks separates other desktop applications, a restricted WebView, the Databricks CLI, and a trusted native core. Sensitive audio stays on the device unless hosted transcription is selected. Transcripts go to cleanup only under policy. Questions and approved context go to Genie One MCP. Approved memory records move between an encrypted local cache and Lakebase. OAuth access tokens and Lakebase credentials remain in native process memory. Workspace leases go only to the selected workspace. A later Databricks Apps adapter uses a separate approved application-origin lease. The diagram classifies secrets, sensitive audio, business content, agentic memory and operational metadata and lists their required controls.
svg.text: Motherbricks: trust boundaries and data flows
The native core is the only component that handles tokens, Lakebase credentials, raw audio and unredacted IPC.
TRUST BOUNDARY 1 — USER DEVICE / OS USER ACCOUNT
arbitrary IPC, hidden device control and raw
system audio. Use a strict IPC allowlist + CSP.
Validate profile name, host and executable.
No token, audio or transcript by default.
No WebView, configuration file, journal or log copy.
Retention, deletion and disk budget required.
Redact content and secrets from telemetry
Security failures block the affected operation.
Allowlisted IPC: commands / status / text / blurb; no secret or raw-audio channel.
Selected profile, user identity, workspace host and grants
Question + approved context; response + deep link
No raw audio. Query rows only on explicit demand.
Cleanup: transcript in / cleaned text out
Optional hosted ASR: audio in / transcript out
Endpoint support and inference logging must be verified.
TLS, least privilege, short-lived credential, retention + deletion.
Same content policy; adapter-specific auth and capabilities.
Separate identity, grants, conversations and memory namespace.
Genie One MCP + Lakebase + Model Services
Reachable only after an explicit CLI profile selection.
New conversations use B. Active A conversations stay on A.
No automatic A-to-B content or memory replication.
Cross-workspace recall or export needs a separate user policy.
F2 OPTIONAL HOSTED ASR — raw audio leaves the device
F6 approved memory + TLS + Lakebase credential

CLI-owned refresh token; cache encryption key

No hidden meeting upload; no cross-workspace reuse by default
write policy; retention; tombstones; export + delete controls

and response IDs; timestamps; status; latency
